evidence.summary: ROLES maps viewer -> {read}, editor -> {read, write}, admin -> {read, write, manage_roles}.
can(role, permission) returns whether the role's permission set contains the permission; an unknown role has no permissions.

set_role(actor_role, target, role) raises PermissionError unless the caller-supplied actor role has manage_roles, then sets target['role'] without checking that the new role exists or who the target is.

features.name: Role-based permissions
features.description: Three roles (viewer, editor, admin), each with a fixed permission set, and one check that answers whether a role may do something.
features.observed_behaviour: can(role, permission) looks the role up in ROLES; unknown roles get an empty set.
features.business_logic: viewer: read. editor: read, write. admin: read, write, manage_roles. Deny by default.
data: role (text) on whatever record represents the user
features.integration: Needs a user store that holds one role per user.

features.name: Admin-only role changes
features.description: An admin changes another user's role.
features.observed_behaviour: set_role raises PermissionError('only admins manage roles') when the actor role lacks manage_roles; otherwise it writes the new role.
features.business_logic: Only manage_roles may change roles. The actor's role is passed in by the caller (trusted). The new role is not validated. No rule about changing one's own role.
features.integration: Needs the caller's identity from a session, not a caller-supplied role.

unknowns: Roster has no user store in the provided code; set_role works on any dict with a 'role' key, so how Roster stores users and their ids is unknown.
